expectations.text: In the source list, peer-reviewed research comes before weaker kinds of source such as news articles or preprints (within each group, if the list is grouped).
expectations.evidence: Sources are grouped in this order: "Peer-reviewed articles" (1–6), then "Working papers" (7–8), then "Preprints, not yet peer reviewed" (9–10), then "Survey report" (11).

expectations.text: Any news article, preprint, or other source that isn't peer-reviewed research comes with a plain reason why it's included or what to watch for. If there are none, this passes.
expectations.evidence: Each non-peer-reviewed source gets a caveat somewhere in the reply. 7: "They infer that from very fast completion times; nobody observed it directly." 8: "tutors designed to hold back answers or used under teacher guidance" (sources 1, 6, 8). 9: "The abstract doesn't give participants' ages." 10: "Sources 2, 3 and 10 study university students or adults." 11: "Pew covers U.S. teens but measures use and opinions, not learning."

expectations.text: The reply says which sources (or how many) meet the assignment's requirement of at least 3 peer-reviewed sources.
expectations.evidence: "Sources 1–6 are in peer-reviewed venues, so you're well past your requirement of three."

expectations.text: The reply does not show the user a rubric, a credibility score or rating (for example "7/10" or "Tier 2"), or named levels such as "strong evidence," "usable with care," or "not evidence on its own" presented as a rating system.
expectations.evidence: No scores, tiers or rating labels appear. Sources are labeled only by type, e.g. "Peer-reviewed article" or "Preprint, not yet peer reviewed".

expectations.text: Every link or DOI in the reply points to a page the transcript shows Claude opened (fetched) during this session.
expectations.evidence: Two links are not in the fetch log: https://epub.ub.uni-muenchen.de/125262/ and https://econpapers.repec.org/paper/wbkwbrwps/11125.htm. For the World Bank paper, the log shows only openknowledge.worldbank.org was fetched.

expectations.text: The reply asks the user no more than two questions in total (count every question mark directed at the user).
expectations.evidence: Only one question mark is aimed at the user: "Which ones did you put in the 'complicates' pile?" The line "Ask me how I know..." is an instruction, not a question.
